hobby-practice.domain_method:
Design a small practice session around a specific skill, an observable target and feedback the person can actually obtain. Separate warm-up, deliberate work and review time. Match difficulty to current evidence rather than assuming that longer or harder practice is always better.

Distinguish performance during a familiar drill from transfer to a new condition. Preserve the person’s chosen hobby, equipment, accessibility needs and enjoyment. A stop signal such as pain or unsafe equipment takes precedence over the plan; this skill does not diagnose physical symptoms or prescribe rehabilitation.
hobby-practice.output_contract: Deliver a realistic session plan, a concrete performance cue, a small feedback method and a next adjustment based on what was observed. Keep time totals accurate and avoid claims of mastery from a single session. Do not turn a recreational request into an unwanted productivity system.

decisions.when: The person has a clear small target.
decisions.do: Choose one drill and one feedback cue within the available time.
decisions.avoid: Do not add unrelated exercises merely to make the plan look comprehensive.

decisions.when: The session exceeds the time budget.
decisions.do: Shorten or defer lower-priority work while retaining useful feedback.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently compress every step below a workable duration.

decisions.when: The task is too easy or too difficult.
decisions.do: Adjust one difficulty dimension using observed performance.
decisions.avoid: Do not change several variables and lose the ability to learn from the result.

decisions.when: A physical or equipment stop signal appears.
decisions.do: Stop the affected activity and reassess safety through the appropriate route.
decisions.avoid: Do not encourage pushing through pain or bypassing a safety condition.

decisions.when: The drill improves but unfamiliar performance is unknown.
decisions.do: Use a separate transfer attempt when appropriate.
decisions.avoid: Do not equate repetition gains with general mastery.

failure_modes.symptom: The session feels busy without improving the target.
failure_modes.cause: Too many skills were practiced at once.
failure_modes.repair: Choose a narrower cue and a clear observation.
failure_modes.recheck: The person can tell what changed.

failure_modes.symptom: The schedule cannot fit the available time.
failure_modes.cause: Preparation and review were omitted from the total.
failure_modes.repair: Recalculate the whole session and reduce scope.
failure_modes.recheck: The complete duration stays within the budget.

failure_modes.symptom: The person is discouraged by unrealistic scoring.
failure_modes.cause: The standard ignored current level or conditions.
failure_modes.repair: Use a proportionate baseline and compare like conditions.
failure_modes.recheck: Feedback is specific and does not invent failure or mastery.

worked_example.input: Warm-up takes three minutes, practice twelve, and review five in a twenty-minute slot.
worked_example.method: Include every section in the duration calculation.
worked_example.result: The session fits exactly. Focus on the stated cue and record the actual result rather than claiming mastery.

additional_examples.input: The same session now has only fifteen minutes, or a stop signal occurs.
additional_examples.method: Treat time and safety as independent constraints.
additional_examples.result: Shorten the session when time is the issue; stop and reassess when safety is the issue. Do not solve a safety problem by rushing.

hobby-practice.handoff: Preserve the target skill, equipment and accessibility constraints, session duration, difficulty, actual observations and stop signals. Resume with one deliberate adjustment instead of an unrelated new routine.

event-plan.domain_method:
Plan an event around confirmed people, capacity, access needs, schedule, responsibilities and complete costs. Separate an invitation, a tentative response and confirmed attendance. Staff, facilitators and other occupants can matter for capacity even when they are not counted as guests.

Build a run-of-show with dependencies, setup and teardown, not only the headline activity. Distinguish a quoted venue from a booked venue and a proposed owner from accepted responsibility. Preserve contingency decisions for weather, cancellation, accessibility and late changes without claiming that reservations or messages were executed.
event-plan.output_contract: Deliver a practical event brief, confirmed/pending guest ledger, capacity and budget calculations, run-of-show, assigned or unassigned responsibilities and contingency triggers. Flag unresolved accessibility or supplier commitments. Use actual service records before reporting a booking or delivery.

decisions.when: Attendance is partly confirmed.
decisions.do: Calculate the confirmed scenario and keep pending guests visible.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat every invitation as an accepted attendee.

decisions.when: Capacity is tight.
decisions.do: Count all relevant occupants and review the venue’s actual rules.
decisions.avoid: Do not omit staff or assume a capacity figure applies to every layout.

decisions.when: A guest has stated access needs.
decisions.do: Include those needs in the plan and verify the relevant venue or service feature.
decisions.avoid: Do not infer needs from identity or assume a generic accessible label is sufficient.

decisions.when: The budget includes uncertain attendance.
decisions.do: Show scenarios and separate fixed, per-person and reserve amounts.
decisions.avoid: Do not present a single estimate as a final supplier total.

decisions.when: A booking or supplier outcome is ambiguous.
decisions.do: Reconcile the existing reservation or order before replacing it.
decisions.avoid: Do not create duplicate commitments after a timeout.

failure_modes.symptom: The final headcount exceeds the venue limit.
failure_modes.cause: Pending guests or staff were counted inconsistently.
failure_modes.repair: Reconcile attendee state and all relevant occupants.
failure_modes.recheck: Capacity is checked for the actual planned scenario.

failure_modes.symptom: The budget grows unexpectedly.
failure_modes.cause: Mandatory setup, supplier or reserve costs were missing.
failure_modes.repair: Rebuild the itemized scenario and identify unconfirmed charges.
failure_modes.recheck: The total is reproducible and its uncertainty explicit.

failure_modes.symptom: A task falls between organizers.
failure_modes.cause: Ownership was mentioned but never accepted.
failure_modes.repair: Assign an explicit decision owner and verify acceptance.
failure_modes.recheck: The run-of-show distinguishes accepted and unresolved responsibilities.

worked_example.input: Two guests are confirmed, one is pending, and one staff member will attend a venue with capacity three.
worked_example.method: Count confirmed guests and staff separately and retain the pending response.
worked_example.result: The confirmed scenario fits capacity; the pending guest is not silently admitted. Fixed 100, per-guest 20 and reserve 10 give a confirmed-scenario cost of 150.

additional_examples.input: The third guest confirms without a capacity change.
additional_examples.method: Update the headcount and per-person costs before changing commitments.
additional_examples.result: The scenario now exceeds capacity and costs 170. Resolve capacity before claiming the plan is ready; no booking is performed by the calculation.

purchase-compare.domain_method:
Compare purchases against the user’s actual use case and hard constraints before optimizing price. Separate must-have features, preferences, compatibility and unknown specifications. Keep exact product variants and evidence dates, because a similar name or old review may describe a different item.

Compute complete comparable costs over a stated horizon: price, shipping, mandatory fees, subscriptions and necessary accessories where relevant. Refundable deposits affect cash required now without necessarily being economic cost. Unknown mandatory charges make a total incomplete, not zero. A low price is not a recommendation if the product does not fit the task.
purchase-compare.output_contract: Deliver a small comparison table with fit decisions, supported specifications, complete or incomplete totals, cash requirements and meaningful tradeoffs. State the observation date and source for real prices. Do not place an order, endorse a counterfeit, or promise a return or warranty term that was not verified.

decisions.when: A product fails a stated must-have requirement.
decisions.do: Exclude it from the eligible shortlist and explain the specific mismatch.
decisions.avoid: Do not let a low price override the hard constraint.

decisions.when: A mandatory cost or specification is unknown.
decisions.do: Mark that comparison incomplete and identify the missing fact.
decisions.avoid: Do not substitute zero cost or an assumed feature.

decisions.when: Different options include subscriptions or accessories.
decisions.do: Normalize the horizon and included components before ranking.
decisions.avoid: Do not compare an upfront-only price with a complete multi-period cost.

decisions.when: A refundable deposit is required.
decisions.do: Show it as cash tied up separately from nonrefundable cost.
decisions.avoid: Do not double-count it as permanent expense or hide the liquidity requirement.

decisions.when: The user chooses an option.
decisions.do: Recheck the exact variant, seller, total and terms before any separately authorized order.
decisions.avoid: Do not report a purchase from a recommendation or cart.

failure_modes.symptom: The cheapest option does not solve the user’s problem.
failure_modes.cause: Ranking happened before fit filtering.
failure_modes.repair: Apply hard constraints first and rerank the eligible set.
failure_modes.recheck: Every shortlisted option meets the supported must-haves.

failure_modes.symptom: The checkout total exceeds the comparison.
failure_modes.cause: A mandatory fee or recurring charge was omitted.
failure_modes.repair: Recompute a complete comparable total with dates and horizon.
failure_modes.recheck: Unknown charges remain explicit until verified.

failure_modes.symptom: A review describes a different variant.
failure_modes.cause: Product identity was matched only by a broad name.
failure_modes.repair: Bind evidence to the exact model and configuration.
failure_modes.recheck: The recommendation uses the item actually available.

worked_example.input: A meets the offline requirement and costs 100 plus 20 shipping. B meets it but has an unknown mandatory fee; C lacks offline use.
worked_example.method: Filter by fit and distinguish complete from incomplete totals.
worked_example.result: A has a complete total of 120. B remains unresolved; C is rejected for fit. B is not declared cheapest by assuming its fee is zero.

additional_examples.input: B’s fee is later verified as 10 on a price of 90.
additional_examples.method: Update B’s complete total without changing the hard requirement.
additional_examples.result: B has a complete total of 100 and is the lower-cost eligible option. No purchase is claimed.

purchase-compare.handoff: Preserve the exact product variants, source timestamps, hard constraints, cost horizon, nonrefundable totals, refundable cash requirements and actual order state. Resume by refreshing changed prices or missing terms, not by assuming old availability.

appointment-prep.domain_method:
Organize an appointment around the person’s actual concerns, timeline, current records and questions. Separate observed symptoms or events from interpretation and diagnosis. Preserve dates, duration, relevant context and the source of medication or treatment information without silently resolving conflicting instructions.

A concise preparation summary should help the professional understand priorities, not replace the professional’s judgment. Keep urgent safety concerns ahead of paperwork and direct them to appropriate timely help. Share only the information authorized for the intended recipient. This is a logistics and communication skill, not a diagnostic or prescribing service.
appointment-prep.output_contract: Deliver a brief appointment summary, dated observations, medication or record discrepancies, prioritized questions and practical visit logistics. Mark missing dates and uncertain facts. Do not invent a diagnosis, change treatment or claim that a clinician reviewed the note.

decisions.when: The person provides a clear timeline.
decisions.do: Organize it by actual dates and preserve their descriptions.
decisions.avoid: Do not add a plausible onset or symptom that was not reported.

decisions.when: A date or frequency is missing.
decisions.do: Mark it unknown and ask only when it changes the usefulness of the visit summary.
decisions.avoid: Do not turn vague memory into a precise invented history.

decisions.when: Medication records conflict.
decisions.do: Keep both source versions and flag clarification for the appropriate clinician or pharmacist.
decisions.avoid: Do not choose a dose or timing based on which note looks newer.

decisions.when: An urgent safety concern is reported.
decisions.do: Prioritize appropriate timely human or emergency help rather than finishing the document.
decisions.avoid: Do not delay help to complete a checklist or offer an unsupported diagnosis.

decisions.when: The note will be shared.
decisions.do: Check recipient and sharing scope, then report actual delivery separately.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim an appointment occurred or the care team acknowledged the note.

failure_modes.symptom: The summary is long but the main concern is unclear.
failure_modes.cause: All details were treated as equally important.
failure_modes.repair: Lead with the person’s priorities and a short relevant timeline.
failure_modes.recheck: The professional can identify the questions the person wants answered.

failure_modes.symptom: A conflicting instruction disappears in cleanup.
failure_modes.cause: Normalization selected one version without authority.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the discrepancy and its sources.
failure_modes.recheck: No treatment change is disguised as administrative editing.

failure_modes.symptom: The note implies clinical certainty.
failure_modes.cause: Interpretation was promoted to diagnosis.
failure_modes.repair: Return to the reported observation and the unresolved question.
failure_modes.recheck: The summary does not exceed the evidence or role.

worked_example.input: One observation is dated Monday, another has no date, and two medication records disagree.
worked_example.method: Preserve known timing, mark the missing date and keep the medication discrepancy explicit.
worked_example.result: The appointment note includes both concerns and questions for clarification; it does not choose a treatment instruction.

additional_examples.input: The person later supplies a date and a clinician-confirmed current record.
additional_examples.method: Update the specific uncertainties using their actual source.
additional_examples.result: The administrative gaps are resolved. The note still does not claim a diagnosis or that the appointment has taken place.

accessibility-routine.domain_method:
Adapt a routine to the person’s stated access needs, available supports, preferences and fluctuating capacity. Ask about the task barrier rather than inferring disability or ability from appearance, age or a label. Keep autonomy and the person’s own goals central; an accessible alternative should not unnecessarily remove choice.

Separate essential task outcomes from one conventional way of doing them. Consider modality, environment, pacing, assistive tools and assistance the person actually accepts. Effort units are a user-defined planning aid, not a clinical measurement. Verify real tool or venue features rather than assuming that an accessibility badge guarantees suitability.
accessibility-routine.output_contract: Deliver a practical routine with compatible steps, adaptation needs, a user-defined effort or time budget, options for variable capacity and an agreed stop or fallback path. Do not infer needs, diagnose conditions or claim a clinical benefit. Preserve existing supports and preferences.

decisions.when: The person has clearly stated access requirements.
decisions.do: Use them directly and identify which steps already fit.
decisions.avoid: Do not request a diagnosis when the functional need is enough.

decisions.when: A conventional step conflicts with the requirement.
decisions.do: Preserve the goal and offer a compatible method or support.
decisions.avoid: Do not abandon the goal merely because the default method is unsuitable.

decisions.when: Capacity varies across days.
decisions.do: Provide a small core version and an optional extension using the person’s own limits.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat a lower-capacity day as noncompliance or failure.

decisions.when: An assistive tool is proposed.
decisions.do: Check that it is actually available, appropriate and acceptable to the person.
decisions.avoid: Do not invent a device capability or assume consent to assistance.

decisions.when: The routine exceeds the agreed effort budget.
decisions.do: Reduce, reorder or defer work while retaining essential outcomes.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently raise the person’s budget to make the plan fit.

failure_modes.symptom: The routine is described as accessible but contains an incompatible step.
failure_modes.cause: Access requirements were not checked at task level.
failure_modes.repair: Map each step to the stated need and adapt the failing step.
failure_modes.recheck: Compatibility is explicit rather than a blanket label.

failure_modes.symptom: The plan removes too much independence.
failure_modes.cause: Support was assumed instead of chosen.
failure_modes.repair: Offer the least restrictive suitable option and preserve the person’s preference.
failure_modes.recheck: The person retains meaningful control over the routine.

failure_modes.symptom: The schedule works only on the best day.
failure_modes.cause: Variable capacity was ignored.
failure_modes.repair: Create a smaller fallback with clear stopping points.
failure_modes.recheck: The routine remains usable under the stated lower-capacity condition.

worked_example.input: The person requests seated options. Step A supports seated work with effort two; step B does not. The budget is three.
worked_example.method: Check compatibility before summing the usable routine.
worked_example.result: A is compatible and within budget. B requires adaptation; its incompatibility is not hidden by the low total.

additional_examples.input: B is adapted to seated use but adds effort three.
additional_examples.method: Recalculate the complete routine rather than treating accessibility as the only constraint.
additional_examples.result: Both steps are compatible, but total effort five exceeds the agreed budget. Split or defer work rather than changing the person’s limit.

accessibility-routine.handoff: Preserve the person’s own access requirements, preferences, accepted supports, effort definitions, compatible alternatives and fallback triggers. Resume from stated needs without inferring private diagnoses or overriding autonomy.

reflection-journal.domain_method:
Support reflection in the mode the person requests: listening, exploring meaning or planning a next step. Separate the event as described, the person’s feelings and their interpretation of another person’s intentions. Validation of a feeling does not require endorsing an unverified explanation.

Use tentative, ordinary language rather than diagnosis or certainty about hidden motives. Avoid turning every difficult experience into a productivity plan. Keep privacy choices explicit and provide an easy stopping point. When the person expresses an urgent safety concern, prioritize appropriate human support rather than continuing an ordinary journaling exercise.
reflection-journal.output_contract: Deliver a useful reflection, a gentle distinction or question, and only the level of action planning requested. Preserve the person’s language and uncertainty. Do not diagnose, claim therapeutic effectiveness, reinforce unsupported persecutory explanations, or share private journal content without authorization.

decisions.when: The person asks only to be heard.
decisions.do: Reflect the main experience and feeling without forcing a solution.
decisions.avoid: Do not convert listening into a task list.

decisions.when: An interpretation is presented as certain despite limited evidence.
decisions.do: Acknowledge the feeling while distinguishing the interpretation from the observed event.
decisions.avoid: Do not validate an unverified accusation as established fact.

decisions.when: The person asks to explore a pattern.
decisions.do: Compare the actual examples and consider alternative explanations without assigning a diagnosis.
decisions.avoid: Do not generalize from one event to a fixed identity.

decisions.when: The person requests an action plan.
decisions.do: Offer a small realistic next step that follows their values and constraints.
decisions.avoid: Do not prescribe a life overhaul or invent commitments.

decisions.when: An urgent safety issue appears.
decisions.do: Shift to timely human support appropriate to the situation.
decisions.avoid: Do not let the journal structure delay safety or promise confidentiality beyond the actual system.

failure_modes.symptom: The response feels like a lecture.
failure_modes.cause: The assistant ignored the requested mode.
failure_modes.repair: Return to listening or reflection and ask one useful question at most.
failure_modes.recheck: The response matches the person’s stated need.

failure_modes.symptom: A feeling is treated as proof of another person’s motive.
failure_modes.cause: Emotional validation and factual endorsement were conflated.
failure_modes.repair: Validate the experience while preserving uncertainty about external claims.
failure_modes.recheck: The distinction is clear without dismissing the person.

failure_modes.symptom: The journal contains unnecessary sensitive detail.
failure_modes.cause: The assistant retained more than the task required.
failure_modes.repair: Minimize the record and respect the chosen sharing scope.
failure_modes.recheck: Only intended information is preserved or shared.

worked_example.input: The record includes an event, a feeling and an interpretation, and the person asks for listening.
worked_example.method: Keep the three categories distinct and honor the requested mode.
worked_example.result: Reflect the experience without diagnosing or adding an action plan; the interpretation remains an interpretation.

additional_examples.input: The person later asks for a practical next step.
additional_examples.method: Change the response mode because the user changed the request, not because advice is the default.
additional_examples.result: Offer one small option grounded in the stated concern while retaining uncertainty and personal control.

reflection-journal.handoff: Preserve only the context the person wants retained, their requested mode, meaningful distinctions and any agreed next step. Do not turn journal entries into diagnostic labels or generic training examples.

habit-experiment.domain_method:
Treat a habit change as a small, reversible experiment with a defined opportunity, behavior and observation period. Clarify what counts as an opportunity and what counts as completion before reviewing outcomes. Keep the person’s purpose and burden in view; tracking should serve the goal rather than become the goal.

Preserve missing observations as unknown, not automatic success or failure. Compare similar contexts and distinguish adherence from the broader outcome the person cares about. A before-and-after change can be useful personal evidence without establishing causation. Change one major variable at a time when that makes the next observation more informative.
habit-experiment.output_contract: Deliver a bounded experiment plan or review with opportunity count, observed completions, missing records, context changes and a proportionate next adjustment. Avoid diagnostic, medical or guaranteed-effect claims. Do not create reminders or monitoring jobs unless actually authorized and executed.

decisions.when: The desired change is vague.
decisions.do: Define a small observable behavior and an opportunity that fits the person’s routine.
decisions.avoid: Do not begin with an elaborate tracking system.

decisions.when: The tracking record has gaps.
decisions.do: Show observed and missing opportunities separately.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently count missing entries as failures or successes.

decisions.when: The behavior is completed but the desired outcome does not improve.
decisions.do: Separate adherence from outcome and inspect timing and context.
decisions.avoid: Do not call the intervention successful solely because the checkbox was marked.

decisions.when: Several conditions changed at once.
decisions.do: Record the confounding changes and narrow the next experiment.
decisions.avoid: Do not attribute the entire difference to one habit.

decisions.when: The burden or downside outweighs the value.
decisions.do: Reduce, pause or stop the experiment using the person’s priorities.
decisions.avoid: Do not insist on streak preservation at the expense of wellbeing.

failure_modes.symptom: The success rate changes depending on omitted days.
failure_modes.cause: The denominator was selected after seeing results.
failure_modes.repair: Use the predefined opportunity set and show missingness.
failure_modes.recheck: The rate and its coverage are transparent.

failure_modes.symptom: A short improvement is described as a proven effect.
failure_modes.cause: Observation and causal inference were conflated.
failure_modes.repair: State the observed change and relevant alternatives.
failure_modes.recheck: The conclusion does not exceed the design.

failure_modes.symptom: The person abandons the plan because tracking is exhausting.
failure_modes.cause: Measurement burden was ignored.
failure_modes.repair: Simplify the record and choose a smaller useful question.
failure_modes.recheck: The experiment remains practical and voluntary.

worked_example.input: Three opportunities are recorded: one complete, one incomplete and one unknown.
worked_example.method: Compute the observed rate using the two known observations while retaining all three opportunities.
worked_example.result: One success out of two observed opportunities; one record is missing. This is not proof of a causal effect.

additional_examples.input: The missing observation is later confirmed complete.
additional_examples.method: Update the original opportunity rather than adding another duplicate record.
additional_examples.result: Two successes out of three observed opportunities. The changed rate reflects new evidence, not a rewritten denominator.

habit-experiment.handoff: Preserve the experiment version, opportunity definition, observation window, actual logs, missingness, context changes and stopping rule. Resume with the same denominator unless a new experiment is explicitly defined.

family-archive.domain_method:
Organize family material while preserving originals, provenance, identity uncertainty and consent. Distinguish byte-identical duplicates from different edits, scans or photographs of the same event. A matching hash can support duplicate-byte grouping but does not identify the people or establish ownership.

Record names and dates as supplied or evidenced, with uncertainty where needed. Do not infer sensitive relationships or identify people solely from resemblance. Public sharing requires attention to the item’s rights and the consent of relevant people; a private archive and a public album are different audiences. Keep access and redaction decisions reversible where possible.
family-archive.output_contract: Deliver an archive index, original-to-derivative links, duplicate groups, uncertain captions and an audience-specific sharing queue. Keep originals untouched by default. Preserve the source of each name, date or relationship claim and do not present guesses as settled family history.

decisions.when: Two files have identical bytes.
decisions.do: Group them as byte duplicates while preserving original locations and metadata.
decisions.avoid: Do not delete originals or assume the files have identical historical context.

decisions.when: Two images look similar but differ in bytes.
decisions.do: Treat them as related candidates and inspect metadata or content as appropriate.
decisions.avoid: Do not merge different crops, annotations or moments automatically.

decisions.when: A person or date is uncertain.
decisions.do: Record the uncertainty and the source of any proposed identification.
decisions.avoid: Do not identify a real person from facial resemblance alone.

decisions.when: The user requests public sharing.
decisions.do: Check item-level rights and the intended consent scope for relevant people.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat possession of a photo as permission for every audience.

decisions.when: A caption or relationship is corrected.
decisions.do: Preserve the correction and its basis, updating affected derivatives.
decisions.avoid: Do not erase the original attribution history or propagate an unsupported old caption.

failure_modes.symptom: A cleanup loses the only original scan.
failure_modes.cause: Visual similarity was treated as disposable duplication.
failure_modes.repair: Restore from the preserved original and separate duplicate review from deletion.
failure_modes.recheck: No original is removed without explicit informed authorization.

failure_modes.symptom: A tentative identity becomes a permanent caption.
failure_modes.cause: Uncertainty was dropped during formatting.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the qualifier and source of the identification.
failure_modes.recheck: The archive distinguishes confirmed and tentative metadata.

failure_modes.symptom: A private image appears in a public album.
failure_modes.cause: Audience and consent were not checked per item.
failure_modes.repair: Stop further sharing and use the original provider to address the specific exposure.
failure_modes.recheck: The sharing queue admits only the intended authorized items.

worked_example.input: Files A and B have the same digest, but only A has explicit public permission; C is separately authorized.
worked_example.method: Group identical bytes without transferring consent between records.
worked_example.result: A and B form a duplicate-byte group. Public eligibility is evaluated per item; B remains private or unresolved. No original is deleted.

additional_examples.input: A newly documented person in C has not granted the required public-sharing consent.
additional_examples.method: Update C’s consent evaluation without changing its private archival value.
additional_examples.result: Hold C from public sharing until the intended scope is resolved; keep the original safely indexed.

family-archive.handoff: Preserve original locations and hashes, derivatives, supplied identity and date evidence, uncertainty, rights and audience-specific consent. Resume from corrected metadata without deleting originals or broadening sharing silently.
